subject: Wellsight MAP: evaluation acceptance criteria and fall-through plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Nguyen <alexandra.nguyen@wellsightlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Wellsight MAP: evaluation acceptance criteria and fall-through plan

Hi Alexandra —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. As promised, I pulled together a short mutual action plan and the high-level acceptance criteria we’d use to validate a successful evaluation. I attached a one-page MAP (wellsight_map_v1.pdf) and a working sheet of the acceptance tests (acceptance-tests.xlsx).

Summary of proposed success criteria (high level):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 750-token average prompt during normal load (measured on our dedicated test harness).
- Throughput: sustain 50 user requests/sec with <5% error rate across 1m sustained window.
- Quality: task-specific correctness/concordance >= 95% on the agreed 2k prompt validation set (we’ll share scoring rubric).
- Security & governance: ability to run inside your VPC with customer-managed KMS and SOC2 evidence provided for our hosted systems.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency traces available to your SREs for the pilot.

Exit gates / fall-throughs (short):
- Blocker: any data-exfiltration signal or configuration that prevents VPC isolation => stop.
- Performance fail: if p95 latency > 300ms or error rate > 10% for two consecutive 15-minute windows => automatic rollback to previous model variant and paging to our on-call.
- Quality fail: if accuracy < 90% on the validation set during canary => pause rollout and schedule root-cause session.

Pilot cadence we propose:
1) Kickoff & integration week (wire up VPC, KMS, test harness)
2) Canary (7 days): run production-weighted traffic with injected validation prompts and the shared test set.
3) Observation (3 days): measure stability and edge-case coverage.
4) Decision: sign-off, extend to full pilot, or deprovision.

Can you review and confirm the criteria above? If it looks good I’ll circulate a slimmed mutual action plan with owners and dates and loop in Karthik for the canary instrumentation details.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): wellsight_map_v1.pdf (1 page MAP), acceptance-tests.xlsx (2k prompt validation set summary)

From: Alexandra Nguyen <alexandra.nguyen@wellsightlabs.com>

Cc: procurement@wellsightlabs.com, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@wellsightlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Wellsight MAP: evaluation acceptance criteria and fall-through plan

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick questions from our side before we sign off on the MAP:

1) Billing model during the canary — is usage counted against a temporary eval agreement or will we get a credit invoice? We prefer a capped eval credit so we can measure cost/performance without surprise billing.
2) Canary rollback mechanics — we need a concrete runbook. If the canary fails, who triggers the rollback and how quickly? Our ops team will need an SLA for rollback execution and confirmation.
3) Test harness — can Redwood run the injected validation set remotely, or do you require us to route traffic through your hosted endpoint? We prefer a VPC-hosted option where the data never leaves our environment.

Tom (cc’d) wants to be sure the acceptance test covers a 95th percentile of edge-case prompts (we’ll share a short list). Also, we may need a two-week pilot instead of seven days depending on our internal release calendar.

If you can provide the rollback runbook and a proposed billing protection (eval credit or capped spend) we can get procurement moving.

Best,
Alexandra Nguyen
Head of Product
Wellsight Labs

Alexandra —

Thanks — answers inline below and I’ve attached a short canary-runbook (canary-plan.pdf).

1) Billing protection: we can run the evaluation under a capped eval credit (RDW eval credit) tied to deal RDW-WSL-0034. We’ll cap at $5k for the canary by default; if you need a different cap we can adjust. Procurement: we’ll issue a credit memo and zero-dollar invoice for initial integration to make PO processing simpler.

2) Canary rollback runbook (high level):
- Trigger: automated alarms in our monitoring (p95 latency, error rate, quality regression) OR manual trigger from your SRE.
- Action: control plane executes a policy-driven failover to the pinned fallback model variant within 90 seconds of trigger.
- Confirmation: post-rollback smoke run (30 minutes) and a rollback confirmation email to both teams.
- Pager: Redwood on-call and SRE contact list included in canary-plan.pdf.

3) Test harness & VPC: we support VPC-hosted deployments for the pilot. For the canary we’ll deploy a private instance in your VPC, run the injected validation set locally (data does not leave your network), and stream aggregated metrics back to the Redwood console (no raw prompts forwarded). Karthik will supply the instrumentation hooks (prometheus metrics + token-level traces) — looping him in here to confirm the technical checklist.

If that looks good, next steps I suggest:
- Lauren to send slimmed MAP with owners/dates by EOD Monday.
- Procurement to issue a PO referencing the eval credit cap and deal id.
- Kickoff call: propose Tue, 08 Jun, 10:00 PT.
